text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement (I): For 
[IMG]
, all three possible structures may be drawn as follows.


[IMG]
Statement (II): Structure III is most stable, as the orbitals having the lone pairs are axial, where the lp – bp repulsion is minimum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{ClF}{}_{3}$, Cl has 7 valence electrons: three form Cl–F bonds and four remain as two lone pairs, giving 5 electron pairs in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement ($\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}$).

The two lone pairs can be placed both equatorial (I), one axial and one equatorial (II), or both axial (III), so all three structures can be drawn and Statement I is correct.

Counting repulsions at $90^{\circ }$: structure I has 0 lp–lp and 4 lp–bp, structure II has 1 lp–lp and 3 lp–bp, and structure III has 0 lp–lp and 6 lp–bp.

An axial position has three neighbours at $90^{\circ }$ while an equatorial position has only two, so lone pairs placed axially (structure III) suffer the largest lp–bp repulsion, not the smallest.

Structure II is destabilised by the $90^{\circ }$ lp–lp repulsion, and structure I has fewer lp–bp repulsions than III, so structure I (T-shaped) is the most stable and Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : The first ionisation enthalpy of group 14 elements is higher than the corresponding elements of group 13.

Statement (II) : Melting points and boiling points of group 13 elements are in general much higher than those of corresponding elements of group 14.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The first ionisation enthalpies ($\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) of corresponding elements are B 801 < C 1086, Al 577 < Si 786, Ga 579 < Ge 761, In 558 < Sn 708 and Tl 589 < Pb 715. From group 13 to group 14 the nuclear charge increases while the added electron enters the same shell, so in every pair the group 14 element holds its electrons more tightly. Statement I is correct.

The melting points (K) are B 2453, Al 933, Ga 303, In 430, Tl 576 for group 13 and C 4373, Si 1693, Ge 1218, Sn 505, Pb 600 for group 14; the boiling points (K) are Al 2740, Ga 2676, In 2353, Tl 1730 against Si 3550, Ge 3123, Sn 2896, Pb 2024. Each group 14 element melts and boils higher than the group 13 element beside it, so Statement II is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Consider the ground state of chromium atom $(Z=24)$. How many electrons are with Azimuthal quantum number $l=1$ and $l=2$ respectively ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ground-state configuration of chromium ($Z=24$) is

$1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{6}3s^{2}3p^{6}3d^{5}4s^{1}$

and not $3d^{4}4s^{2}$, because the half-filled $3d^{5}$ subshell is extra stable owing to its symmetrical distribution and maximum exchange energy.

Electrons with $l=1$ ($p$ orbitals): $2p^{6}+3p^{6}=6+6=12$.

Electrons with $l=2$ ($d$ orbitals): $3d^{5}=5$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement (I) : Molal depression constant $\mathrm{K}_{f}$ is given by $\frac{\mathrm{M}_{1}\mathrm{RT}_{f}}{\Delta \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{fus}}}$, where symbols have their usual meaning.

Statement (II) : $\mathrm{K}_{f}$ for benzene is less than the $\mathrm{K}_{f}$ for water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement-I

Molal depression constant $\mathrm{k}_{f}=\frac{\mathrm{M}_{1}\mathrm{RT}_{f}^{2}}{\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text{fus}}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{k}_{f}=\dfrac{\mathrm{M}_{1}\mathrm{RT}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\left [\frac{\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{fus}}}{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}}\right ]} \\ \mathrm{k}_{f}=\dfrac{\mathrm{M}_{1}\mathrm{RT}_{f}}{\Delta \mathrm{S}_{\text{fus}}} \end{array}$

Hence statement-I is correct

but $\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$ for benzene $=5.12\frac{{}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}}{\text{molal}}$

$\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}$ for water $=1.86\frac{{}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}}{\text{molal}}$ Hence statement- II is incorrect

The IUPAC name of the following compound is:

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The chain containing the OH carbon, the C=C and the C≡C has seven carbons: $\mathrm{HC}\equiv \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$.

The principal characteristic group $-\mathrm{OH}$ (suffix -ol) must receive the lowest locant; it is on C-4 from either end.

The multiple bonds then receive the lowest locant set, which is $\{1,6\}$ from either end. When this ties, the double bond is given the lower number, so numbering starts at the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=$ end: C=C at C-1 and C≡C at C-6.

The name is hept-1-en-6-yn-4-ol. Options (A) and (D) wrongly cite OH as the prefix hydroxy although it is the principal group, and option (C) gives the triple bond the lower number in a tie.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Half life of zero order reaction $\mathrm{A}\to$ product is 1 hour, when initial concentration of reactant is $2.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}{}^{-1}$. The time required to decrease concentration of A from 0.50 to $0.25\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For zero order reaction

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Half life}=\dfrac{\mathrm{A}_{\mathrm{o}}}{2\mathrm{k}} \\ 60\min =\dfrac{2}{2\mathrm{k}} \\ \mathrm{k}=\dfrac{1}{60}\mathrm{M}/\min  \end{array}$

Now

$\begin{array}{l} A_{t}=A_{o}-kt \\ t=\dfrac{A_{o}-A_{t}}{k} \\ =\dfrac{0.5-0.25}{1/60} \\ 0.25\times 60 \\ t=15\min  \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: The incorrect relationship in the following pairs in relation to ionisation enthalpies is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The ionisation enthalpy of an ion $\mathrm{M}{}^{k+}$ is the energy to remove one more electron from it, that is, the $(k+1)$th ionisation enthalpy of M.

(A) $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ ($[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}$) must lose an electron from the stable half-filled $3d^{5}$ set, while $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ ($[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{6}$) loses its paired sixth $d$ electron and becomes $3d^{5}$. So $\Delta _{i}H_{3}$ of Mn ($\approx 3248\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is greater than $\Delta _{i}H_{3}$ of Fe ($\approx 2957\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}<\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ is incorrect.

(B) An electron leaves the more positive $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ less easily than $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}$: $\Delta _{i}H_{2}\approx 1509<\Delta _{i}H_{3}\approx 3248\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, so $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}<\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ is correct.

(C) $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}$ and must break the half-filled set, while $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{5}4s^{1}$ and loses its $4s$ electron: $\Delta _{i}H_{2}$ of Cr ($\approx 1592\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) exceeds that of Mn ($\approx 1509\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$), so $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{+}<\mathrm{Cr}{}^{+}$ is correct.

(D) $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ carries a higher charge and has the half-filled $3d^{5}$ set, so $\Delta _{i}H_{4}$ of Fe is far above $\Delta _{i}H_{3}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}<\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: ' $X$ ' is the number of electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals of the most stable complex ion among $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]^{3+},[\mathrm{FeCl}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})_{3}]^{3-}$ and $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$. The nature of oxide of vanadium of the type $\mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{X}}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Among the four Fe(III) complexes, $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]{}^{3-}$ is the most stable because each oxalate ion is a bidentate chelating ligand (chelate effect).

$\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$ and oxalate is a weak-field ligand ($\Delta _{o}<P$), so the complex is high spin (magnetic moment about $5.9\text{BM}$) with the configuration $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$.

Thus $X=3$ and the oxide is $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$, with vanadium in its low +3 oxidation state.

The vanadium oxides change from basic $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ to less basic $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}$ to amphoteric $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ as the oxidation state rises, so $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$ is basic.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Consider the given data :

(a) $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\to \mathrm{HCl}.10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\Delta \mathrm{H}=-69.01\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

(b) $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\to \mathrm{HCl}.40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\Delta \mathrm{H}=-72.79\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Choose the correct statement :
options: The heat of dilution for the $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{HCl}.10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ to $\mathrm{HCl}.40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})$ is $3.78\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
Dissolution of gas in water is an endothermic process.
The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent.
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b).
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From the given information

$\Delta \mathrm{H}$ is negative so it means dissolution of gas $\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})$ is exothermic.

$\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\to \mathrm{HCl}.10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\text{..... (1)}$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{H}_{1}=-69.01\dfrac{\mathrm{kJ}}{\mathrm{mol}} \\ \mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{g})+40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\to \mathrm{HCl}.40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\text{..... (2)} \end{array}$

$\Delta \mathrm{H}_{2}=-72.79\frac{\mathrm{kJ}}{\mathrm{mol}}$

Hence heat of solution depends upon amount of solvent

By equation ............. (2) $-$ equation ........... (1)

$\mathrm{HCl}.10\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}+30\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\ell )\to \mathrm{HCl}.40\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

So Heat of dilution $=-72.79-(-69.01)$

$=-3.78\frac{\mathrm{kJ}}{\mathrm{mol}}$

Hence option (1) is incorrect.

For heat of formation reactant should be in elemental form hence option (4) is incorrect

text: The correct order of $[\mathrm{FeF}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}]^{3-},[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_{4}]$ and $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}]^{2-}$ complex species based on the number of unpaired electrons present is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The number of unpaired electrons follows from the oxidation state of the metal and the field strength of the ligand.

$[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$ and $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so the complex is high spin ($\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{2}$) with 5 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$ and with weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ the complex is high spin ($t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$) with 4 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$ and strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs all eight electrons in four 3d orbitals, giving square planar $\mathrm{dsp}^{2}$ with 0 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$: Ni(0) is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$ and strong-field CO shifts the 4s electrons into 3d, giving $3d^{10}$ (tetrahedral $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$) with 0 unpaired electrons.


[IMG]

The order is therefore $5>4>0=0$, that is $[\mathrm{FeF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}>[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}>[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}=[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$; option (B) fails because it ranks the two diamagnetic nickel species as unequal.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

[IMG]

The dipeptide x therefore gives alanine and glycine on hydrolysis; among the options only alanine-glycine is made of these two amino acids.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The amount of calcium oxide produced on heating 150 kg limestone ( $75%$ pure) is
$_________ kg. ($Nearest integer)

Given: Molar mass (in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of Ca-40, O-16, C-12
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}\to \mathrm{CaO}+\mathrm{CO}_{2} \\ \text{mass of}\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}=\dfrac{150\times 75}{100}=112.5\mathrm{kg} \\ =112500\mathrm{g} \\ \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}}=1125 \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{So moles of}\mathrm{CaO}=1125 \\ \text{mass of}\mathrm{CaO}=\dfrac{1125\times 56}{1000}=63\mathrm{kg} \\ \text{Correct answer}\Rightarrow 63 \end{array}$

text: A metal complex with a formula $\mathrm{MCl}_{4}\cdot 3\mathrm{NH}_{3}$ is involved in $\mathrm{sp}^{3}\mathrm{d}^{2}$ hybridisation. It upon reaction with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ solution gives ' $x$ ' moles of AgCl . Consider ' $x$ ' is equal to the number of lone pairs of electron present in central atom of $\mathrm{BrF}_{5}$. Then the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{BrF}{}_{5}$, Br has 7 valence electrons, 5 of which form the Br–F bonds, leaving 1 lone pair; so $x=1$ and only 1 mol of AgCl is precipitated per mole of complex.

With one ionisable $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ and six-coordination ($sp^{3}d^{2}$), the complex is $[\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}]\mathrm{Cl}$, an octahedral complex of the type $[\mathrm{Ma}{}_{3}\mathrm{b}{}_{3}]$.

$[\mathrm{Ma}{}_{3}\mathrm{b}{}_{3}]$ has two geometrical isomers: facial (fac), with the three $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ on one triangular face of the octahedron (every Cl–M–Cl angle $90^{\circ }$), and meridional (mer), with the three $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ in one plane containing the metal (two of them trans to each other).

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
The molar conductance of an infinitely dilute solution of ammonium chloride was found to be $185\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and the ionic conductance of hydroxyl and chloride ions are 170 and $70\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, respectively. If molar conductance of 0.02 M solution of ammonium hydroxide is $85.5\mathrm{S}\mathrm{cm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, its degree of dissociation is given by $x\times 10^{-1}$.
The value of $x$ is $__________ . ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ }\text{of}\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}=185 \\ (λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}}+(λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{Cl}^{-}}=185 \\ (λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}}=185-70=115\mathrm{Scm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\ (λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}}=(λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}}+(λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{OH}^{-}} \\ =115+170 \\ (λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}}=285\mathrm{Scm}^{2}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \text{degree of dissociation} & =\dfrac{(λ_{\mathrm{m}})_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}}}{(λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\circ })_{\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{OH}}} \\ =\dfrac{85.5}{285} \\ =0.3 \\ =3\times 10^{-1} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
$x\mathrm{mg}$ of $\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}($ molar mass $=58)$ is required to be dissolved in 1.0 L of water to produce a pH of 10.0 at 298 K . The value of $x$ is $________ mg. ($Nearest integer)

(Given : $\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}$ is assumed to dissociate completely in $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the mass of Mg(OH)₂ that needs to be dissolved to achieve a pH of 10.0, follow these steps:

Given:

pH = 10

Therefore, pOH = 14 - pH = 4

[OH⁻] = 10⁻⁴ M

First, calculate the number of moles of OH⁻ ions:

Number of moles of OH⁻ = 10⁻⁴

Since Mg(OH)₂ dissociates completely in water, from one mole of Mg(OH)₂, you get two moles of OH⁻:

Number of moles of Mg(OH)₂ = (10⁻⁴) / 2 = 5 × 10⁻⁵ moles

Next, calculate the mass of Mg(OH)₂:

Molar mass of Mg(OH)₂ = 58 g/mol

Convert the number of moles to mass:

Mass of Mg(OH)₂ = (5 × 10⁻⁵ moles) × (58 g/mol) = 2.9 × 10⁻³ g

Convert to milligrams: 2.9 × 10⁻³ g = 2.9 mg

Therefore, the calculated mass of Mg(OH)₂ required is approximately 2.9 mg.
